title: Throughput and latency sweep for FP8/INT8 mixed-mode across bursty batched long-horizon traffic
creator: Maya R. Ortiz
description:
Objective: Run an end-to-end validation sweep evaluating FP8, INT8 and hybrid mixed-mode quantization profiles to measure throughput, median/95/99 latency and accuracy degradation across representative production-like traffic patterns. Emphasis is on interactions between batching logic (microbursts vs steady streams), KV-cache warm/cold behavior, and very long context windows (4k–16k tokens).

Scope and goals:
- Quant variants: FP8 (E4M3/E5M2 configurations), INT8 symmetric/asymmetric per-channel, and hybrid FP8-INT8 fallbacks.
- Calibration workflows: evaluate static calibration (percentile/clamp), KL-divergence and MSE calibrators using our representative dataset (wiki-corpus + internal docs sampling v1). Capture calibration stability across sampling seeds.
- Accuracy validation: perplexity on language-model holdout, and semantic task regression tests (zero-shot classification and NLI) to bound quality loss. Success criteria: perplexity delta <= 2.0% relative to FP32 and downstream F1 drop <= 1.0% for high-sensitivity tasks.
- Performance axes: batch sizes [1,4,8,32,64,128], context lengths [512,2048,8192,16384], request patterns { steady, periodic microburst (10x rps for 2s), prefix-heavy (long shared prefix reuse), cold-start KV-cache }. Measure throughput (tokens/s), median/95/99 latencies, and per-token cost delta.
- Hardware targets: A100-80GB and H100-80GB nodes (single-GPU and multi-GPU per pod configurations) with kernel selection flags used by runtime-1.22.
- Harness: use benchmark harness 'quant-sweep-harness' (internal GH), instrumented for per-request traces (OpenTelemetry) and Grafana dashboards. Save raw traces and result CSVs to s3://redwood-bench/quant-sweep/ENG-531007/.

Acceptance criteria (quantitative):
- Mixed-mode FP8 yields >=1.35x throughput vs FP32 at batch >=32 without exceeding 20% increase in 99th percentile latency at context <=8k.
- INT8 option must show stable tail latency (<25% regression) and no more than 2.5% perplexity increase.
- If either quant mode violates quality thresholds, validate if calibration tuning (percentile clipping or KL) recovers accuracy within 3 iterations.

Planned experiments and measurements:
1) Baseline: FP32 runs across all axes to record baseline P50/P95/P99 and throughput.
2) FP8 profiles: run E4M3 and E5M2 variants with our standard calibration pipeline and an alternative MSE calibrator.
3) INT8: symmetric per-channel and asymmetric with outlier-clamp heuristics.
4) Hybrid: allow token-type based fallback (attention layers FP8, MLP INT8) to observe best cost/quality tradeoff.
5) KV-cache scenarios: cold-start vs warm cache pre-warmed by synthetic prefix workloads; measure cache miss penalties and recovery windows.
6) Microburst resilience: 10x request bursts for 2s and observe queuing, batching behavior, and fallback kernel invocation rates.

Artifacts to produce:
- CSV matrix of throughput/latency across (precision, batch, context, pattern, hw).
- Per-run traces and histograms uploaded to S3.
- Grafana dashboard link for interactive analysis and a short confluence page summarizing findings and recommended runtime defaults.
- Runtime PR (if kernel flags or batching heuristics need tuning) and an RFC for hybrid fallback policy if beneficial.

Risks and mitigation:
- Calibration overfits to our sampled dataset: mitigate by holding out an internal 'edge' set and running A/B checks.
- KV-cache artifacts amplify tail latency in long-context cases: add prewarm scripts and evaluate small warmup windows.
- Mixed-mode numerical instability in certain layers: add per-layer quant-sensitivity profiling and enable layer-level fallback in runtime for investigated suspects.

Next steps / timeline:
- Week 1 (this doc): finalize experiment matrix and test harness (owner: Liam).
- Week 2: run baseline FP32 and initial FP8 E4M3/INT8 symmetric runs across A100. Collect first-pass CSVs (owner: Maya + bench team).
- Week 3: run H100 sweep, calibration seed sensitivity, and microburst scenarios. Draft confluence findings and perf dashboard.
- Week 4: decide on runtime changes; open PR(s) and schedule canary on a dedicated pool if needed.
